# Ayman Alawwad

PMO Manager · Portfolio & Program Governance
Turning strategy into governed delivery leaders can see.
More than ten years across technology, infrastructure, construction and government environments in Saudi Arabia, from a national-scale technology rollout to building a firm's Center of Excellence.
Location: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

## Executive bio
Ayman Alawwad is a PMO and portfolio management leader with more than ten years of experience across portfolio governance, strategic initiatives, technology, infrastructure, construction and government environments in Saudi Arabia. He combines hands-on delivery with portfolio-level governance to strengthen accountability, improve executive visibility and support effective decision-making.

At TAHAKOM he led the end-to-end delivery of national-level smart traffic violation detection systems across multiple Saudi cities, working with government and private-sector stakeholders, multi-vendor environments and cross-functional teams of more than 17. Earlier, he delivered a SAR 28 million infrastructure project for the Ministry of Education two weeks ahead of schedule, and launched a Center of Excellence that supported his firm's upgrade from 3rd- to 1st-grade classification.

He has earned the PMP®, PMI-RMP® and P3O® certifications, and was selected among 60 of 1,200 candidates for an eight-month High Potential leadership program with modules from MIT, the National University of Singapore, ESCP Business School and Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management. He holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University.

## Profile
I am a PMO and project/program management professional with more than ten years of experience across portfolio governance, strategic initiatives, technology, infrastructure, construction and government environments in Saudi Arabia.
My work combines hands-on project delivery with portfolio-level governance, bridging strategy and execution, strengthening accountability, improving executive visibility and supporting effective decision-making.
I have managed and delivered projects and portfolios exceeding SAR 500M, working with government stakeholders, executives, multidisciplinary teams and more than 28 suppliers across complex delivery environments.

## Signature figures
- SAR 500M+: Projects and portfolios managed and delivered
- 10+: Years across portfolio governance and delivery
- Top 5%: Selected 60 of 1,200 for an eight-month leadership program

## How he leads
- Bridge strategy and execution: I combine hands-on delivery with portfolio-level governance, so the priorities set by leadership reach the teams doing the work. In practice: Kept business requirements and technical delivery aligned on national-level systems.
- Give leaders a clear view: Executive reporting and governance exist to support decisions. I build the visibility that lets leadership decide with confidence. In practice: Executive reporting, RAID management and risk registers with regular reporting.
- Structure + flexibility = results: Not every project fits one box. I run Agile, Waterfall or hybrid delivery according to what the work needs. In practice: 5+ hybrid projects delivered, and Product Owner on 2+ Agile projects.
- Make accountability shared: Government stakeholders, executives, teams and suppliers each own part of delivery. Governance makes that ownership clear. In practice: Multi-vendor environments managed for performance and compliance; 28+ suppliers evaluated.

## Mandates
- Establishing PMO governance: PMO governance frameworks that make accountability, standards and decisions visible. In practice: Launched a Center of Excellence that standardized processes and documentation.
- Portfolio & program management: Projects and portfolios exceeding SAR 500M, managed and delivered across sectors. In practice: Giga-scale infrastructure and technology deployments for public and private clients.
- Strategy execution & prioritization: Strategic alignment and prioritization that keep delivery tied to the organization's objectives. In practice: Prioritized conflicting deadlines across 3+ concurrent projects.
- Risk & RAID management: Risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies tracked and reported. PMI-RMP® earned in 2022. In practice: Monitored risks and maintained risk registers with regular reporting.
- Executive reporting & stakeholders: Reporting and stakeholder management with government entities, executives and multidisciplinary teams. In practice: Managed stakeholders across government and private sector entities.
- Vendor & supply governance: Multi-vendor environments managed for performance and compliance. In practice: Supplier evaluation frameworks; 28+ suppliers evaluated and approved.

## Governance architecture
- Strategy: Strategic alignment and prioritization
- Portfolio: Portfolio governance and executive reporting
- Program: Program management and cross-functional delivery
- Project: Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery, with risk, cost and schedule under control
- Operations: Operational readiness and business value

## Journey
### I. Foundations (2016 – 2021), Khazaz Engineering Office
I started in quality assurance, auditing projects against quality and safety standards, then moved into project management.
As Assistant Project Manager I launched the firm's Center of Excellence, prepared bids for public infrastructure tenders and contributed to raising the firm's classification from 3rd to 1st grade. By 2020 I was managing projects end to end and reporting performance to senior management.
In 2018 I also trained with The Royal Commission for Riyadh City on the Al-Ddoho revival project, with an overview of the Riyadh Metro.
- Quality Assurance Specialist, Khazaz Engineering Office (2016 – 2017)
- Assistant Project Manager, Khazaz Engineering Office (2017 – 2020)
- Trainee Civil Engineer, The Royal Commission for Riyadh City (2018)
- Project Manager, Khazaz Engineering Office (2020 – 2021)

### II. Delivery at scale (2021 – 2022), Tatweer Buildings Company
I led the full lifecycle of a SAR 28M infrastructure reconstruction project for the Ministry of Education, coordinating internal teams, contractors and the client, and resolving technical and contractual issues along the way.
It was delivered two weeks ahead of schedule and within budget, in full compliance with quality and safety standards.
- Project Manager, Tatweer Buildings Company (2021 – 2022)

### III. National programs (2022 – 2026), TAHAKOM
At TAHAKOM I moved from engineering into leading national-level technology programs. As Project Engineer I worked on the standards behind delivery, evaluating suppliers, writing technical guidelines and system designs, and keeping risk registers current.
As Project Manager I led the end-to-end delivery of smart traffic violation detection systems across multiple Saudi cities, with cross-functional teams of 17+, multi-vendor environments and hybrid delivery.
I was honoured for the accomplishment of 2023 targets, and in 2025 I was selected among 60 of 1,200 candidates for the company's High Potential leadership program.
- Project Engineer, TAHAKOM (2022 – 2024)
- Project Manager, TAHAKOM (2024 – 2026)

## Impact
### Nationwide rollout of smart violation detection systems
TAHAKOM · 2024 – 2026 · Project Manager
Mandate: Lead the delivery of new smart traffic violation detection systems across multiple cities in Saudi Arabia, from concept to operation.
Complexity: National-level systems supporting traffic enforcement operations, with government and private-sector stakeholders, multiple engineering streams and a multi-vendor environment. Alongside it, giga-scale infrastructure and technology deployments for high-profile public and private clients, with conflicting deadlines across 3+ concurrent projects.
How he led:
- Ran delivery in a hybrid Agile/Waterfall model, acting as Product Owner on 2+ Agile projects
- Led cross-functional teams of 17+ members
- Kept business requirements and technical delivery aligned
- Managed vendors for performance and compliance, and prioritized conflicting deadlines
Result:
- 5+ hybrid projects delivered
- Site operations launched on time nationwide
- Solutions implemented on time, with resource and budget optimization

### Raising quality through supplier and design standards
TAHAKOM · 2022 – 2024 · Project Engineer
Mandate: Bring consistency to the materials and designs behind mega infrastructure and smart traffic enforcement projects.
Complexity: Civil and power materials from many suppliers, engineering teams that needed a shared design approach, and government stakeholders to keep informed throughout.
How he led:
- Established supplier evaluation frameworks and approved 28+ suppliers for civil and power materials
- Authored two technical guidelines and seven system designs that standardized the design approach
- Tested, diagnosed and validated new technologies
- Maintained risk registers with regular reporting
Result:
- Material rejection rates reduced by 40%
- Shorter procurement cycle time and better vendor quality
- Less rework and stronger quality assurance

### SAR 28M infrastructure rehabilitation for the Ministry of Education
Tatweer Buildings Company · 2021 – 2022 · Project Manager
Mandate: Deliver a SAR 28M infrastructure reconstruction project for the Ministry of Education, covering site reconstruction, MEP systems and handover documentation.
Complexity: A full project lifecycle with contractors, internal teams and a government client, and the technical and contractual issues that reconstruction work brings.
How he led:
- Managed the full lifecycle, from planning and execution to monitoring and closure
- Led communication across internal teams, contractors and the client
- Resolved technical and contractual issues to keep delivery moving
- Held the project to quality standards and timelines
Result:
- Delivered two weeks ahead of schedule and within budget
- Full compliance with quality and safety standards

### A Center of Excellence that helped lift a firm to 1st grade
Khazaz Engineering Office · 2017 – 2020 · Assistant Project Manager
Mandate: Standardize how the firm ran its projects, documentation and bids, and align them with its strategic plan.
Complexity: Public infrastructure tenders that demanded accurate bills of quantities, and a firm working toward a higher contractor classification.
How he led:
- Launched the internal Center of Excellence to standardize processes and documentation
- Prepared BOQs and bidding packages for public infrastructure tenders
- Led training, documentation and audit preparation
Result:
- Contributed to the firm's upgrade from 3rd to 1st-grade classification
- Better bid alignment with project goals, with higher contract win rates and budget accuracy
